title: Metabolomics-guided analysis combined with network pharmacology and molecular simulations reveals the mechanism of JHT in treating septic intestinal dysfunction.
authors: Deng, Rou; Hu, Yingying; Luo, Jielian; Cui, Xiayu; Huo, Chenxing; Zhang, Runze; Zhu, Liang; Zhang, Wen; Fang, Bangjiang
one_liner_zh: 该文研究中药JHT治疗脓毒症肠功能障碍的代谢组学与网络药理学机制，核心为炎症信号通路与代谢重编程，无蛋白质-DNA互作体系、无结合建模，亦无AI或物理模拟方法聚焦于核酸-蛋白互作，与本课题无关。
abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Jinhong Tang (JHT), recorded in Surgery of Traditional Chinese Medicine, is a famous modern prescription for acute abdomen. Our previous study demonstrated that JHT can improved the immune function and organ function of patients with sepsis, achieving favorable clinical outcomes. However, the basis of these effects and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. We aimed to explore the efficacy and mechanism of JHT in reducing septic intestinal dysfunction. METHODS: Active components of JHT, identified in prior HPLC-IT/MS analyses, were used for network pharmacology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations to predict key therapeutic targets and pathways. To functionally validate these predictions, untargeted metabolomics of colonic tissues was performed followed by pathway enrichment analysis to assess metabolic alterations. A cecal ligation and puncture (CLP)-induced septic mouse model was used to evaluate the effects of JHT on intestinal dysfunction in vivo. Histological changes were assessed via hematoxylin-eosin (HE) staining, and serum inflammatory cytokines were quantified using ELISA. Gene expression of key metabolic enzymes was measured by real-time quantitative PCR (qPCR), and protein levels of signaling molecules were analyzed by Western blotting. RESULTS: Network pharmacology suggested that JHT may exert therapeutic effects through the AMPK/SIRT1/NF-kappaB signaling pathway. Metabolomics revealed that JHT reversed sepsis-induced disruptions in glycolysis, tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle, and tryptophan metabolism, while regulating mitochondrial-associated energy metabolism. In vivo, JHT significantly reduced serum TNF-alpha, IL-6, and IL-1beta levels compared to the model group. HE staining showed reduced mucosal edema, attenuated inflammatory infiltration, and preserved colonic architecture. Western blot analysis demonstrated upregulation of AMPK, phosphorylated AMPK (p-AMPK), and SIRT1, along with downregulation of p-NF-kappaB and pro-inflammatory cytokines. Glycolysis-related enzymes PFKFB3 and LDHA were also significantly reduced in JHT-treated animals. CONCLUSION: JHT alleviated septic intestinal dysfunction by modulating the AMPK/SIRT1/NF-kappaB signaling axis, suppressing inflammatory responses, and reprogramming abnormal glycolytic metabolism. These findings supported the multi-target, multi-pathway mechanism of JHT and provided a pharmacological basis for its application in the treatment of sepsis-associated intestinal injury.
abstract_zh: 民族药理学相关性：金糖（JHT），记载于《中医外科学》，是治疗急腹症的著名现代方剂。我们前期研究表明，JHT可改善脓毒症患者的免疫功能和器官功能，取得良好临床疗效。然而，这些效应的基础及其潜在机制仍不清楚。本研究旨在探讨JHT减轻脓毒症肠道功能障碍的功效及机制。方法：利用前期HPLC-IT/MS分析鉴定的JHT活性成分，进行网络药理学、分子对接和分子动力学模拟，以预测关键治疗靶点和通路。为功能验证这些预测，对结肠组织进行非靶向代谢组学分析，随后进行通路富集分析以评估代谢变化。采用盲肠结扎穿刺（CLP）诱导的脓毒症小鼠模型，评估JHT对体内肠道功能障碍的影响。通过苏木精-伊红（HE）染色评估组织学变化，并使用ELISA定量血清炎症细胞因子。通过实时定量PCR（qPCR）测量关键代谢酶的基因表达，通过Western blotting分析信号分子的蛋白水平。结果：网络药理学提示JHT可能通过AMPK/SIRT1/NF-kappaB信号通路发挥治疗作用。代谢组学显示，JHT逆转了脓毒症诱导的糖酵解、三羧酸（TCA）循环和色氨酸代谢紊乱，同时调节线粒体相关能量代谢。在体内，与模型组相比，JHT显著降低血清TNF-alpha、IL-6和IL-1beta水平。HE染色显示黏膜水肿减轻、炎症浸润减弱，结肠结构得以保留。Western blot分析显示AMPK、磷酸化AMPK（p-AMPK）和SIRT1表达上调，同时p-NF-kappaB和促炎细胞因子下调。JHT处理动物中，糖酵解相关酶PFKFB3和LDHA也显著降低。结论：JHT通过调节AMPK/SIRT1/NF-kappaB信号轴、抑制炎症反应和重编程异常糖酵解代谢，减轻脓毒症肠道功能障碍。这些发现支持JHT的多靶点、多通路机制，并为其在脓毒症相关肠道损伤治疗中的应用提供了药理学基础。
